title: Pilot live triage — seller scripting & metrics (draft v0.2)
content:
Purpose: a compact, live-facing reference for Sellers/SEs running pilot demos or responding to a customer incident during a pilot. Goals: keep the customer confident, preserve pilot momentum, and collect evidence (metrics/logs/trace ids) that we can hand to CE/SE/eng for root cause and follow-up.

Audience: seller on call (SE optional), pre-sales engineer, account owner. Use in live demos, on-call triage with a prospect, or post-incident follow-up.

Status: rough draft. Meant to be printed as a 1–2 page crib sheet or used as a speaker notes sheet for SOS calls.

Quick TL;DR script (first 60s)
- Greeting (30s): "Thanks—we’ll keep this short. I’m Sam from Redwood, with Ethan on engineering. We’ll triage quickly so you can keep moving and we’ll follow with a written summary + next steps within 24 hours."
- Immediate reassurance (15s): "This looks like a pilot artifact; service is still up and we have fallbacks. We’re not at production risk yet."
- Action & ask (15s): "Can you confirm the request id or demo step where you saw the issue? If you don’t have it, please share the timestamp and your user role so we can match traces."

Live triage checklist (what the seller does in the call)
1) Collect context (explicit): customer account, pilot region, model name + version, endpoint name, request id or approximate timestamp, user persona, number of concurrent users, an example prompt that triggered the issue.
2) Check quick metrics (we script these values):
   - Console / Live dashboard: P50 / P95 latency (last 5 min) — show P50 and P95 in console.
   - Token rate / reqs per second (last 1m) — show current throughput.
   - Error rate / 5xxs in last 15m (count).
   - Model fallback events (last 24h): any fallbacks to low-cost variant?
   - Billing spike indicator: tokens burned over threshold?
3) Triaging classification (pick one):
   - A: User prompt / expected output quality issue (content/regression). Ownership: product + QA. Quick seller script: "This looks like an output-quality issue — we’ll capture the prompt + answer and run the evaluation harness, then propose a mitigation (prompt tweak or model variant) within 48 hours."
   - B: Latency spike (degraded p95 but success responses). Ownership: SRE/serving-runtime. Script: "We’re seeing a P95 jump — ask for concurrent request count, and confirm if the customer used long-context calls during the spike."
   - C: Errors/5xxs (failed responses). Ownership: infra/ops + SE. Script: "We have failures — please grab a sample request id and stacktrace (if available) and we’ll raise an incident to get an immediate remediation and fallback points."
   - D: Cost / unexpected token burn. Ownership: GTM + billing ops. Script: "We’ll pause heavy batch runs and collect the token histogram and model selection history. We can recommend a quantized variant or caching policy for the pilot."

Live commands & what to show the customer (screen/scripted items)
- Show Live Console -> Route: Model usage -> Last 5 min -> highlight P95 and recent errors.
- Show Request Sample: copy a specific request payload + response (redact PII).
- Show Routing Policy: where their requests went (region/variant).
- Show Token spend trend for the session window.
- If you can’t access console, ask customer to produce a request id and timestamp and promise to follow up with screenshots.

Canned seller lines for common objections
- "It’s a pilot, not production — this is expected behavior we instrument for. We’ll own the follow-up and deliver a concrete remediation plan in 24–48 hours."
- Latency objection: "We can bound the P95 with a dedicated pool or switch to a lower-context variant; for pilots we usually set a burst pool to keep interactive demos smooth."
- Cost objection: "We can apply caching, prefix KV reuse, or a quantized variant to reduce per-token cost for the pilot while preserving fidelity."
- Security/data concern: "We can run this in private/vpc mode with KMS integration and sign NDAs for any logs you share — we’ll outline a data handling plan."

Quick math snippets (for live rebuttals)
- Token cost estimate: "Your demo ran ~3 calls/min * 2,000 tokens avg * 24 hours = 144k tokens/day. At $0.0004/token (example), that’s ~$57.60/day — we can show how caching reduces that to ~x."
- Latency rollback: "If P95 becomes >1000ms we recommend +Dedicated pool (targets sub-500ms) or reduce model to small-llm-v1 for UI flows."

Evidence capture template (what to paste into ticket/slack after call)
- Subject: Pilot triage — <customer> — <date/time>
- Collected: account, region, endpoint, model+version, request-id(s), timestamps, approximate concurrent requests, session token volume, screenshot links.
- Impact class: A | B | C | D (see triage classification)
- Immediate actions taken on call: (e.g., turned on fallback, increased concurrency limit, paused batch job)
- Owner & next steps: (assign to SE/CE/engineering)

Post-call follow-up templates (email to customer)
- Short: "Thanks for the time today. We captured the issue and are investigating. Summary: category=A (quality). Next steps: run evals on the prompt, suggested temporary mitigation: model variant X or prompt change Y. We will deliver a follow-up by <date/time>."
- Detailed: include the evidence capture block, linked trace ids, and recommended mitigations with estimated time-to-fix.

Roleplay snippets (for SE practice)
- Customer: "Generated hallucination about legal liability."
  Seller: "Sorry about that — can you send the exact prompt? We’ll run that prompt through our eval harness and if it’s a model truth/regression we’ll propose a model swap or guard rails in 48 hours."
- Customer: "P95 spiked to 2.3s during demo."
  Seller: "Understood. Can I show the live console? If confirmed, we’ll temporarily route traffic to the lower-latency variant and open an ops ticket to investigate the root cause."

Known limitations & TODOs (notes to self)
- TODO: add one-click console links for: recent traces, token histogram, per-route latency.
- TODO: include pre-built Kibana queries / dashboards for SEs.
- Limit: This crib-sheet assumes seller has console access; if not, fallback to evidence capture and promise screenshots.

Appendix: Quick URL bookmarks for the seller
- Console (Pilot overview): https://console.redwood.ai/pilot/<account>
- Trace explorer: https://console.redwood.ai/traces
- Billing demo histogram (example): https://console.redwood.ai/billing/demo-hist
- Internal slack channel: #gtm-pilot-surge

Notes to self: keep language non-technical in customer-facing lines; for internal handoffs be explicit about ownership (SRE, serving, infra, billing). This version focuses on demos & pilots; build a sibling crib-sheet for Dedicated/on-prem incident flows.
